title: Kth Largest in a Stream
statement:
Build a tracker that reports the kth largest value seen so far each time a number is added.

Contract
- `new Solution(k, initial)` starts with the values in `initial` (any order, possibly empty) and a fixed rank `k >= 1`. Do not modify `initial`.
- `add(value)` records one more value and returns the kth largest of every value recorded so far, counting repeated values separately.
- At least `k` values exist after every `add`, which requires `initial.length >= k - 1`. Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `k < 1` or when `initial` has fewer than `k - 1` values.
- Values may be negative. `k` may be much smaller than the number of recorded values.

Examples
- With `k = 2` and `[10, 3, 7]`, adding `4, 12, 8, 15` returns `7, 10, 10, 12`.
- With `k = 1` and no starting values, adding `-5, -9, 2` returns `-5, -5, 2`.
- With `k = 2` and `[6, 6]`, adding `6, 1, 9` returns `6, 6, 6` because repeated values count separately.
hints: Only the k largest values can ever be the answer; everything smaller can be forgotten.
Keep exactly those k values in a structure that exposes its smallest member cheaply, because that member is the kth largest.

Use a min-heap capped at size k: a new value enters only if the heap is not full or it beats the heap's minimum, which then leaves. Intended complexity: O(log k) per add and O(k) space. The workload keeps k fixed, so a run of n adds measures as O(n) time and O(1) space.
inputSyntax: Input: k, the starting values and the values to add, separated by semicolons, for example: 2; 10 3 7; 4 12 8 15
